newsitem.title: USA: Meredith to buy four television stations.
newsitem.headline: Meredith to buy four television stations.

text.p: Meredith Corp said Friday that, pending Federal Communications Commission approval, it will acquire four television stations from First Media Television L.P., a private company owned principally by the Marriott family.
Meredith said the cash purchase price for the First Media assets is $435 million, which it will pay with a combination of cash and debt.
The stations are WCPX in Orlando, Fla., KPDX in Portland, Ore.-Vancouver, Wash., KFXO in Bend, Ore., and WHNS serving Greenville, S.C.-Asheville, N.C.

"We are enthusiastic about the value the First Media stations will add to our company and our opportunities in these outstanding markets. Orlando, Portland and Greenville-Asheville fit our broadcasting goal of owning and operating stations with network and geographical diversity," Wlliam Kerr, president, said in a statement. "Moreover, these stations will be especially good additions to our television lineup because they are in growth markets."
Meredith Broadcasting Group now includes seven television stations in Phoenix, Kansas City, Nashville, Orlando, Las Vegas, Flint-Saginaw, Mich., and Ocala-Gainesville, Fla.

Because FCC regulations prohibit ownership of more than one television station in a single market, Meredith said it must divest either its existing Orlando station, WOFL-TV, or its soon-to-be-acquired station there, WCPX.
"Taking into account tax, market and other considerations, our desire is to own one of the Orlando stations and trade one of them for one or more stations with high growth opportunities," Kerr said.

Assuming the company trades an Orlando station for a station in a market serving at least a like number of households, Meredith's planned acquisition of the First Media television stations will move its Broadcasting Group from under five percent to nearly eight percent of U.S. households, Meredith said.
